title: EU Injections Begin from Record-Season Lows, US Refill Off to an Early Start
hook: EU storage at 29% entering injection season — the steepest refill climb in years. US inventories start the season above the 5-year average, with EIA forecasting a comfortable 4,015 Bcf by October.
authorWord: On track: US cushion is comfortable. EU's refill cliff is real — every week of LNG flows matters.
author: Blaise 🧮
details:
EU Storage (AGSI+, 10 Apr): 29.04% full (328.65 TWh) — up from 28.0% on 3 Apr as injections resumed across most sites. Germany sits at just 22.8%, the Netherlands at a perilous 5.3%, and France at 23.1%. On the higher end, Italy holds 43.6% and Spain 59.5%, but neither can substitute for the core northwest buffer. The EU Gas Coordination Group confirmed constant injections since early April as a positive signal, but hitting the 90% November 1 target requires ~785 TWh of net injections over ~28 weeks — a pace not seen since 2022's emergency refill.

US Storage (EIA): Working gas ended the 2025-26 withdrawal season at just over 1,900 Bcf, 3% above the five-year average. The first injection of the season came in at +36 Bcf for the week ending Mar 27 — two weeks earlier than the 5-yr norm and 40 Bcf above the comparable week's average. The April STEO projects inventories reaching 4,015 Bcf by end of October, well above the 5-yr average, thanks to production growth and limited new LNG export capacity coming online in 2026. Henry Hub sits near $2.90/MMBtu, supported by LNG and data-center demand floors.

Trajectory check: The transatlantic divergence is stark. US refill math is comfortable — an average ~67 Bcf/week gets to 3,800+ Bcf by Nov 1, and early-season injections provide a cushion. The EU faces a much tighter path: at 29%, roughly 71 percentage points of capacity must be refilled in ~28 weeks, demanding sustained LNG and pipeline inflows at record spring/summer rates. Any disruption to LNG supply or an early cold snap next winter would test Europe's margins severely.
